messages:
alex: Heads up — ran a perf pass on Mistral-8x7B this morning, found a regression in 99p tail for long sliding-window contexts. baseline (old kernel selector): ~85ms 99p, new selector + rope-scaling heuristics: ~130ms 99p. Root cause looks like KV cache churn due to mask alignment + kernel choice when seq_len ~ 2.5k.
maria: ugh. any flamegraphs / traces?
alex: uploading snippet, but quick summary: when we hit the sliding window fast-path (we change start_idx frequently) the kernel chooser prefers a tiled GEMM kernel that expects contiguous KV pages. On roam of the start offset, we end up patching allocations and invalidating tile metadata so we get serial copy work on the critical path.
cheng: can you paste the repro command? I'll run on my dev GPU.
alex: repro: ```/opt/redwood/bin/runner --model mistral-8x7b --seq_len 2500 --prompt-file tests/long_prompts.json --profile=kv,mem,kernel_selector --runs=50```
alex: attached profiler output shows spikes aligned with `tile_metadata_update()` and `kv_page_rebind()` calls. Also RoPE scaling code path does a fallback in a few layers due to mismatched max_position_embeddings, which forces per-request re-init in the runtime.
zane: I saw similar earlier when we bumped max_pos to 4096 for some Mixtral configs — we had to prewarm the cache. Could prewarming or eager tile layout fix this?
maria: prewarm might help but doesn't address the kernel choice flip-flop. Both are contributing. Guess: kernel_selector uses cost model that only sees seq_len and head_dim, not current cache contiguity / offset patterns.
cheng: patch idea: enrich kernel selector state with a cheap heuristic: if (kv_offset % tile_size != 0) => prefer copy-friendly kernel or streaming kernel that tolerates misaligned KV. Also add a short-term cache of recent offsets so we don't oscillate on rapid sliding windows.
alex: exactly. plus: special-case when model.max_position_embeddings != runtime_window -> avoid on-the-fly RoPE recompute. We should failback to a compat ropescale table precomputed for standard windows.
zane: on the batching side, noticed that our batcher coalesces by model variant but not by offset pattern. For sliding windows we should prefer to group requests with similar start_idx to increase KV hit rate. Could add a hash on (start_idx // window_stride).
maria: small POC patch incoming: two parts — kernel_selector change + batch grouping by window shard. Will run ab test on dedicated pool.
bench-bot: perf test queued: job id rb-4821. Estimated runtime 2h. Results will post in #eng-runtime.
cheng: also let's add a telemetry metric: `kv_rebind_count` per request and `kernel_selector_flip_rate` to quantify. If flip_rate > 0.2 we flag and force stable kernel for N seconds.
alex: agree. Also config snippet for selector heuristic (draft): ```{"selector": {"prefer_copy_kernel_on_misaligned_kv": true, "alignment_tile_size": 256, "stable_hold_seconds": 3}}```
maria: run the POC and if we get >=30% reduction in kv_rebind_count and 2x reduction in 99p tail we'll roll to canary.
zane: I'll monitor memory churn and make sure we don't regress p50 on short contexts.
alex: thanks team. I'll attach the profiler tarball to the bench-bot job and post a summary once rb-4821 completes. :thumbsup:
